newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council, parliament still at odds over novel foods.
newsitem.headline: Council, parliament still at odds over novel foods.

text.p: The European Parliament and Council of Ministers remain deadlocked over the draft directive on novel foods and will have to extend their negotiations under the conciliation procedure, Council sources said on Tuesday.
The two sides, who met on Monday, failed to make any progress on their main conflict -- how to label genetically engineered or other new foods brought onto the market, they said.

The parliament delegation continued to fight for its Amendment 55 to the Council's common position on COM(93)631, which says that labels should inform consumers any time the composition, nutritional value or intended use of a novel food differs from those of a conventional food.
The Council, supported by the Commission, argues that approach is too restrictive and wants such labels only when there is a "significant" difference between the two products.
The two sides also remain divided over when labels should indicate that a product contains a genetically modified organism, the sources said.
They decided to call it a day after only 90 minutes of discussion, stressing that fresh ideas were needed and calling for informal contacts, the Council sources said.

They scheduled a formal conciliation committee meeting for November 27 -- one day after the end of the initial six-week deadline for completing their negotiations. That means they will have to extend their talks for another two weeks, as allowed under conciliation procedure rules.

If they still fail to agree, the Council could agree by qualified majority to confirm its original common position or to take up the parliament's amendments. The parliament could, however, veto that text by an absolute majority, or 314, of its members.
